g.text: What the scheduler is given, and what it decides
CPU scheduler
schedule()
thread behaviour, measured
I/O-bound: short bursts, blocks often
CPU-bound: uses every slice to the end
niceness, set by the user or admin
nice -20 (greedy) ... 0 ... +19 (nice)
static: it does not change on its own
the trigger
slice expired, thread blocked or yielded,
a higher-priority thread woke up
which thread runs next, on which CPU
its time slice: how long before it is
asked to leave
updated priorities (dynamic):
threads that block often go up,
threads that hog the CPU go down
small time slice: fast turn-taking, responsive,
but many context switches -- interactivity
large time slice: fewer switches, more work
per second, but a longer wait in line -- throughput
one knob, two goals
The inputs are what the threads do and what the admin asks for; the outputs are who runs, for how long, and with what priority.
